novel_features.name: Hydrated chronological inventory
novel_features.description: See every chat in chronological order with turn counts, time span, and freshness — not just titles.
novel_features.rationale: The list API returns no counts (verified empirically); a local SQLite hydration cache computes them incrementally by update watermark.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when you need a real index of conversations by time and size instead of scrolling the sidebar.

novel_features.name: Verified-complete extraction
novel_features.description: Extract an entire conversation with a completeness proof against the live tree state.
novel_features.rationale: The detail API's has_next_page can report false on truncated windows (empirical); cursor-walking to current_node with verification is the only safe extraction.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an export must contain every message — audit, migration, or feeding another agent.

novel_features.name: Long-thread outline
novel_features.description: Map a long thread into titled sections at each of your prompts, with timestamps and anchors.
novel_features.rationale: ChatGPT's own table of contents derives purely from user messages (verified via React inspection); the same derivation over the API needs no extra endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before reading a 100-message thread — get the structure first, then pull only the section you need.

novel_features.name: Section-sliced extraction
novel_features.description: Extract just part of a long conversation by section number or message anchors.
novel_features.rationale: Outline anchors index into the message array, so slicing is a local range computation no API provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to pull one topic out of a sprawling thread without extracting everything.

novel_features.name: Dual-mode search
novel_features.description: Search message content server-side by default, or offline over your synced archive.
novel_features.rationale: The Ctrl+K global search endpoint returns federated message-level hits; the synced SQLite store mirrors it for offline work.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this to find the exact conversation and message containing a phrase, fresh or from cache.

narrative.headline: Your ChatGPT history as a queryable local archive — verified-complete extraction, outlines, and search no other tool has.
narrative.value_prop: Turn conversations into a chronological index with real turn counts and spans, extract any thread completely with a completeness proof, navigate long threads by outline, and search message content server-side or offline. Sessions survive token expiry via cookie re-mint and optional Codex auth import.
narrative.auth_narrative: No API key. Import your chatgpt.com browser session once (cookies) and the CLI mints fresh bearer tokens itself — cookies outlive the 10-day token TTL, so the session keeps working. Alternatively point it at your existing codex login (~/.codex/auth.json). Send commands are experimental and browser-gated: they consume only legitimately issued authorization and fail with a clear error otherwise.

quickstart.comment: Health check without touching the network
Chronological inventory with turn counts and span
See the structure of a long thread first
Server-side message search with compact output

troubleshoots.fix: Bearer is missing/expired: run chatgpt-pp-cli auth import again; cookie-only access returns masked empty responses.
Turnstile-gated: sends are experimental and browser-gated; refresh authorization via chatgpt-pp-cli auth import and retry, or use the web UI.
Re-run with --full-refresh to cursor-walk the conversation from scratch; the page_info flag can under-report.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you need chronological inventory of conversations with real metadata, verified-complete single-thread extraction (JSON or readable transcript), long-thread outlines and section slicing, or message-content search (server-fresh (find) or offline (search)). Ideal for archiving, auditing, feeding conversation context to other agents, and navigating very long threads. Use 'use chatgpt' or 'run chatgpt' for these workflows.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to delete, rename, or archive conversations — destructive management is deliberately excluded
Do not use it for bulk attachment or project backups — dedicated exporters cover that
Do not use it for deep-research or agent-mode chat parity — use the web UI or pi-gpt
Do not expect headless send reliability — sends are experimental and browser-gated
